title: IL-23 p19 blockade (risankizumab) in Crohn's disease
question: Would blocking the IL-23 p19 subunit (IL23A) with risankizumab help patients with moderate-to-severe Crohn's disease?

summary.text: Randomised phase 3 trials show that risankizumab, a p19-directed IL-23 antibody, improved clinical remission and endoscopic response over placebo in induction and maintenance in moderate-to-severe Crohn's disease, including patients who had failed biologics. The benefit is partial, and the evidence is sponsor-funded and placebo-controlled.

keyFindings.text: Induction (ADVANCE/MOTIVATE): all co-primary week-12 endpoints met with 600 and 1200 mg IV; MOTIVATE (biologic-failure) CDAI remission 42%/40% vs 20% placebo, endoscopic response 29%/34% vs 11%.
Maintenance (FORTIFY, withdrawal design): SC 360 mg q8w gave week-52 CDAI remission 52% vs 41% and endoscopic response 47% vs 22% against withdrawal to placebo.
Open Targets association 0.61 is dominated by clinical evidence (0.99); literature and expression evidence are low, so the support is largely pharmacological.
Risankizumab is annotated as an IL-23 inhibitor targeting the p19-containing IL-23 (Q9NPF7).

opposingEvidence.text: Benefit is incomplete: in FORTIFY, 180 mg did not significantly beat withdrawal on stool-frequency/abdominal-pain remission (p=0.124). Absolute induction remission gains were about 15-22 points, so most patients remained out of remission. Worsening Crohn's disease was among the common adverse events.

contextDifferences.text: Induction populations differed: ADVANCE included conventional-therapy and biologic failures, while MOTIVATE included only biologic failures. FORTIFY enrolled induction responders only, so maintenance results do not apply to non-responders.
ChEMBL lists Crohn's disease at max phase 3, while the overall max phase is 4. This reflects the annotation only and says nothing about efficacy.
No experimental risankizumab-IL23A complex was found. The AlphaFold model's pLDDT reflects structural confidence, not disease relevance.

limitations: Pivotal evidence comes from sponsor-funded (AbbVie) trials. Records for the same study (registry and paper) are not independent.
Trial comparators were placebo or placebo withdrawal. No head-to-head result was retrieved.
The registry results table for NCT03104413 had duplicated or mislabelled US vs global rows, so numbers were taken from the publication.
Only the primary publications were read. Real-world and long-term safety reports were not examined.
Risankizumab blocks the p19 subunit of IL-23, but this work did not isolate p19-specific effects from IL-23 pathway effects generally.
unknowns: Comparative efficacy against ustekinumab, anti-TNF and other IL-23 agents in Crohn's disease.
Durability and long-term safety beyond 52 weeks.
Efficacy in specific subgroups such as perianal fistulizing and pediatric disease.
Which patients respond, since no predictive biomarker was identified.
nextQuestions: How does risankizumab compare with ustekinumab or adalimumab in head-to-head Crohn's disease trials?
What are the long-term (>52 weeks) safety and durability data from open-label extensions?
What do real-world cohorts show for patients who failed prior biologics?
Is there genetic or biomarker evidence that predicts response to p19 blockade?
